title: ICC + Liquidity + Location
hook: Every concept has a different job.

launchpad.outcome: Keep liquidity and location as optional context, never as ICC requirements.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Are all four required to call something ICC?

beats.title: ICC: bullish sequence developing
beats.line: Where is price in the directional sequence?

slides.title: Turn the context off

asks.prompt: Are all four required to call something ICC?

options.label: Yes, structure, location, liquidity AND ICC
options.feedback: You’re adding context to the definition. Would the ICC still exist without the sweep?

options.label: No. Context can help. It isn’t a requirement.
options.why: Exactly. No confluence score. No checklist of everything you’ve learned.

asks.prompt: A clean bullish ICC with no FVG, no equal lows and no sweep. Invalid?

options.label: Invalid, no confluence
options.feedback: ICC doesn’t need an FVG or a sweep to exist.

options.label: Still ICC
options.why: Context supports understanding. It doesn’t define ICC.

slides.principle:
CONTEXT CAN SUPPORT UNDERSTANDING
WITHOUT BECOMING ANOTHER BOX TO CHECK.

slides.quote: No 4/5 confirmations. No 90% setups. Every concept you learned has a job, and none of them is “required box”.

slides.prompt: Why don’t we turn every concept into an ICC requirement?
slides.modelAnswer: Because each concept answers a different question. Liquidity, location and FVGs can support a read, but ICC exists without them. Adding them all as requirements is method bloat.

takeaways: Structure, location, liquidity, ICC: four jobs.
Context helps; it never defines ICC.
remember: Context can support understanding without becoming another box to check.
